author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement (via IGN) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible for a payment.

title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices

author: Callum Self
description:
When Dragon’s Dogma 2 launched back in 2024, it quickly became one of my favorite RPGs of all time. I still look back on it with fondness, and time hasn’t changed my opinion. The chaos of climbing a beast that should crush you with a gentle push of a finger and stabbing away at its weak points alongside your party cannot be beaten. It’s one of the most satisfying combat mechanics in gaming. The impressive-looking Dark Arisen expansion promises to bring improvements alongside a new tale set in the frosty region of Norgan, and by simply wishlisting the DLC on Steam, you could be one of the lucky winners of a Steam Deck OLED.

Dragon’s Dogma 2 may not be one of the best RPGs in many players’ eyes, earning the game a general ‘Mixed’ rating on Steam. However, it’s one of my personal favorites. It’
title: Wishlist Dragon’s Dogma 2 Dark Arisen And You Could Win A Steam Deck OLED

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Like most big movies these days, the upcoming Resident Evil movie from Weapons director Zach Cregger will have its own dedicated popcorn bucket, and now it's been revealed, at least for one theater chain.

People who see Resident Evil at a Regal theater will be able to buy a popcorn bucket themed after an organ-transport bag like the one Austin Abrams' character has in the movie. The popcorn bucket can hold a large order of popcorn and the fine print states that it does not come with a beating heart like the one in the promotional image below. Phew. Pricing for the bucket was not announced.

Tickets for the Resident Evil movie went on sale today, September 1, and today is also the day that Cregger
title: Resident Evil Movie Popcorn Bucket Is Gross But Fitting

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Netflix has confirmed that GTA 6's recent "extended look" trailer was the streamer's most-viewed title overall last week, drawing 31.1 million views.

The trailer was labeled an "English-language film" by Netflix, and it was No. 1 by that designation in 87 of 93 regions globally that Netflix's tracks (via Variety).

The GTA 6 trailer
title: GTA 6’s Extended Look Trailer Seemingly Paid Off For Netflix With Massive Viewership

description:
While Halloween is drawing nearer, the clock is ticking before Epic Games reveals this year's Fortnitemares event, which will carry Fortnite through spooky season with haunting new skins, bosses, weapons, and points of interest on the map. Until that drops, though, there is another way to get your Fortnitemares fix if you happen to be visiting Universal Studios in Orlando or Hollywood.

This year's Halloween Horror Nights (HHN) event has continued the recent trend of gaming properties having a major presence. The past few years have seen The Last of Us, Fallout, and Five Nights at Freddy's brought to life, thanks in no small part to the popularity of the live-action adaptation
title: Fortnitemares Is A Spooky Dream Come True At Universal’s Horror Nights

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 infamously launched in December 2020 in such a poor technical state that Sony took the rare move to remove it from the PlayStation Store. Thousands of people refunded the game. CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has now reflected on this, saying it "was for sure wrong" to launch the game in that state, but he pushed back against the theory that the studio did so to appease investors who wanted to see financial returns.

Speaking to
title: Releasing Cyberpunk 2077 In Its Poor State “Was For Sure Wrong,” CD Projekt Admits

description:
September marks the start of Pokemon Go's latest season, Twilight Trails, and the mobile game is ushering it in with a number of events and Pokemon debuts this month. 

A host of Mega Pokemon are returning once more as part of the Mega Ascension event, which will lead into the big Go Fest Mega Finale on September 5-6. Later in the month, the dark-type Pokemon Maschiff and Mabosstiff will make their debut, and a new Mega-Evolved Pokemon will star in another Super Mega Raid Day.

On top of that, players can look forward to new Raid bosses and Spotlight Pokemon this month, as well as a Community Day classic starring the fan-favorite dragon Pokemon Gible. You can read more about September's biggest Pokemon Go events below.

author: Eric Frederiksen
description:
The original Metroid and Castlevania both turn 40 years old this fall. As the two series most responsible for creating the “metroidvania,” we’re taking this occasion to take a comprehensive view of the popular genre. This is Metroidvania Week.

When many people pick up a controller to play a game, they're looking for one thing above all others: escapism. A break from the real world. There's no better way to do that than to immerse yourself in another world. Getting lost in a completely fictional world is true escapism. These days, open-world games like Cyberpunk 2077, Red Dead Redemption 2, and the most recent Legend of Zelda games do a lot of the work here, giving us maps full of icons to wade through. But the original escapist games came in the form of search-action games, colloquially known as metroidvania games by their f
title: Metroidvania Games Were The Original Open-World Games

description:
The latest batch of removals from Xbox Game Pass have been announced, and some heavyhitters are leaving soon. After The Witcher 3 was removed in August, another CD Projekt Red game, Cyberpunk 2077, is leaving the service on September 15.

Cyberpunk 2077 was added to Game Pass in March this year, so it may have had a six-month deal, given that it's leaving this month.

description:
It's the start of a new month, and right on cue, Microsoft has revealed the first wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass in September. The upcoming batch isn't too massive, but it does include a day-one release that competitive gamers will want to check out, along with more titles for Xbox Game Pass Premium. Inversely, Game Pass will be losing some pretty big titles this month, with Cyberpunk 2077 leading the wave of departures.

Kicking things off today is Shelldiver, an incremental game about a turtle fishing for jellyfish and then selling its catch at its adorable little store. On September 3, Speedrunners 2 launches as a day-one game. T

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Weapons and Barbarian director Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie releases this month, and tickets are now on sale. If you don't want to pay full price, and you meet a certain requirement, you can get a ticket for a whole lot less than normal.

T-Mobile members in the US can score a ticket to Resident Evil for just $5 through Atom Tickets. As relayed by Wario64, subscribers can visit the T-Life mobile app on September 15 to get a discounted ticket.

That is three days before the Resident Evil movie arrives on September 18, though Thursday night screenings on September 17 are also taking place.

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
If you've played a Grand Theft Auto game before, then you are probably familiar with the series' sprinting mechanic. Rather than clicking the left analog stick like in most other games, you have to either hold or mash a face button. It's annoying, less intuitive, and feels like a relic of the past, and luckily, Rockstar apparently agrees: Grand Theft Auto 6 is doing away with it.

As shared by the Italian YouTuber MikeShowSha, you will now click the analog stick in order to sprint. It's a welcome change for muscle memory if nothing else, as anything other than clicking the analog stick feels odd in 2026. We've occasionally seen other game series, like Halo, adjust control schemes over time to fit more modern standards, though usually the option for the old-style controls is available in these
title: GTA 6 Removes The Series’ Worst Feature

"I try not to think about it," Nelson told IGN. "You’re aware of it, of course. But I think we just have to try and make something that we feel is innovating on what

description:
Chronicles: Medieval is a sandbox RPG that puts players in the commanding role of a medieval army, providing a strong mix of action and strategy. GameSpot was able to preview a hands-off demo and speak with senior game designer Gareth Bourn and lead producer Sam Millen about this ambitious medieval sandbox experience set in 14th-century Europe, where there is an exciting amount of freedom and an impressive attention to detail.

Developer Raw Power Games has created a massive action-strategy game, which features large-scale tactical battles and real-time combat. The game is set during the age of the Hundred Years' War, and while the developer spent a lot of time researching for historical a
title: Chronicles: Medieval Provides An Impressive Sandbox For Players To Write Their Own History

author: Callum Self
description:
I went into the Onimusha: Way of the Sword demo completely blind. I had never played any of the previous games in the series, nor did I know what to truly expect. I simply downloaded it and gave it a try. After playing through it with a beaming smile on my face, dismembering demons and having a good ol’ time, this might be one of the best action games since Elden Ring. Better yet, you can join in on the fun with a great preorder discount ahead of launch.

From the opening moments, I was hooked. You play as legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi as you traverse a dark fantasy take on Kyoto, facing rival samurai, demons, and even more threats that the full game will offer. Even though it’s a 25-year-old series, with the last entry launching back in 2006, there’s no requirement to play previous games. Capcom has already said that Way of the Sword is a fr
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Could Be My Favorite Action Game Since Elden Ring, And There’s A Preorder Deal

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
As Sony marches towards its all-digital future, the company is now arguing in a class-action lawsuit that it doesn't mislead customers into purchasing digital licenses for games, instead of actual ownership of the product.

In a filing in California's Northern District Court made last month (and spotted by Game File), Sony claims that "reasonable consumers would not be misled" when shopping on its storefront. The court overseeing the case against Sony is currently evaluating whether it should proceed to arbitration, as plaintiffs argue that Sony doesn't properly disclose the nature of digital purchases on its platforms.
title: Sony’s Digital Game Ownership Argument Is Another Attack On Consumer Rights

description:
What's next for Double Fine following its split from Microsoft and Xbox? A whole lot, as the Psychonauts developer has multiple projects that it wants fans to vote on--including Brutal Legend 2, if you have a spare $100 million lying around.

The studio is currently seeking a more modest $400,000 on Kickstarter to fund its next project--with only a single stretch goal of $100 million--and at the time of writing, has secured $288,000 in pledges. title: I Am Begging One Cool Billionaire To Take Up Double Fine’s Offer To Fund Brutal Legend 2

To address the elephant in the room--yes, some of the DLSS 5-infused creations are horrific. Final Fantasy's Cloud looks like something straight out of a

author: Miri Teixeira
description:
There's no denying that Afterworld is a traditional grand strategy game in many ways--big foggy maps, territorial clashes, macro and micro decision-making--but its end-of-the-world scenario presents an opportunity for Paradox Studios to elevate the genre further still. Even in the brief glimpse we had during a hands-on play session at Gamescom, a number of differences are already showing. 

For a start, Afterworld has a very clear focus on lore-building, which is something the more historical games often take for granted. If you're playing as a Roman General or a post-industrial capitalist, the player tends to know what happened before that point, as a rough approximation of historical events can be summed up in an info screen before moving on. Afterworld is very clearly the outlier: Taking place some 100 years after a mysterious fictional apocalyptic event known only as The Fall, there's a lot to unpack.
title: Paradox’s New Grand Strategy Game Is More Survival-RPG Than You’d Expect

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Ananta's developers are hoping that players will become emotionally invested enough in the game's characters to want to part with their cash.

The upcoming free-to-play open-world action game introduces stories as the story progresses, and when we went hands-on with the game at Gamescom last week, the story missions were its strongest point. Helping two cute little anime characters to stealthily flee a mansion was engaging, I did care about their welfare, and I wanted to help them to stay safe--but is that enough to want to part with my money?

In Ananta, there's an emphasis on allowing players to spend time with the game's characters and become familiar with their lives and personalities. According to the developers, that relationship is intentional, and serves to ensure that players want to spen
title: Ananta Developers Are Counting On You Getting Attached To Its Characters

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
CD Projekt Red recently confirmed that the long-awaited RPG The Witcher 4 is targeting a release in 2028, and that timing has led many to wonder if the Polish developer will offer the game on a disc. After all, Sony is ending support for physical PlayStation discs in 2028 and Microsoft is expected to ditch discs, too.

CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski told The Game Business that the studio has "no influence" on what companies like Sony and Microsoft choose to do with regards to supporting discs.
title: The Witcher 4 Probably Won’t Be On A Disc, But Dev Teases Physical “Feelies” Of Some Type

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The start of a new season in Marvel Snap is almost here, and in September, everything you know about your favorite superheroes is being thrown out of the window. This month, developer Second Dinner is drawing inspiration from the 2014 crossover series, Axis: Inversion. This storyline saw the Avengers, X-Men, and several supervillains team up to take down the Red Skull, who had recently powered up by stealing the brain of the deceased Charles Xavier, eventually evolving into Red Onslaught--don't worry, Charles eventually got better.

After the Scarlet Witch and Doctor Strange wove a spell that accidentally reversed the moral compass of everyone in the vicinity, the Inversion era of Marvel Comics began, resulting in heroes dipping into their darker sides and villains embracing the light--for a few months, at least. Marvel S
title: Marvel Snap’s New Season Flips Heroes And Villains, Making One Card Obscenely Overpowered

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Murals might look like a stylish take on the Hades roguelike formula at first glance, but Disney Illusion Island developer Dlala Studios isn't aiming to copy Supermassive's homework. Instead, the studio is looking to put its own spin on the genre, as it fuses dark fairy tales and hews closer to the action-first approach of modern-day Doom and Diablo. One other big difference in Murals is that it'll offer a customizable approach to difficulty, as Dlala Studios says it wants to prioritize player fun over punishing runs--unless you're into that kind of thing.

"There are difficulty selectors, and you can kind of tweak some of the individual settings," Dlala CEO, Aj Grand-Scrutton, said
title: This New Roguelike Wants To Make Its Difficulty More Welcoming
